title: Datto RMM ransomware and antivirus alerts
volume: Ransomware: none on a normal day. Antivirus alerts come with updates and reinstalls, a few a week across an MSP's clients.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Two custom detection rules for Datto RMM, on the third-party alert records the library's Datto RMM parsers write from its Global Webhooks. They make a detection when the Ransomware Detection monitor fires, and when the antivirus status monitor raises an alert. Each rule matches sensor type Datto RMM only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's Datto RMM parsers, and point a Datto RMM Global Webhook at HTTP Ingest with the alert payload in the parser entry. Then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.
- The rules need the Ransomware Detection and antivirus status monitors in the sites' monitoring policies.

How it works:
- The parsers write the monitor's alert category, such as Ransomware or Antivirus, the device as the target host, and raised or resolved as the status.
- Both rules take raised alerts only, so a resolved alert makes no second detection.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 4 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 24 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take.
- The webhook payloads went to HTTP Ingest one per request as JSON, as a Global Webhook sends them.

Known gaps:
- Webhook alerts carry no time, so the detection's event time is when HTTP Ingest received it.
- The antivirus rule can't tell protection turned off from definitions out of date: read the alert's message.
